articles.title: The Gulf states fear renewed war after the midterms
articles.description: While many people in the U.S. have been focused on midterm elections, officials from the Gulf Arab countries met over the weekend at the Ritz Carlton in Bahrain’s capital. Their hope: to stop a new round of U.S. attacks on Iran.This episode was produced by Christopher Harland-Dunaway. Our director is Michael Levitt. articles.title: United Arab Emirates says military solutions offer no quick off-ramps to crisis with Iran
articles.description: The United Arab Emirates hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough in Qatar-led mediations to prevent a new confrontation between the U.S. and Iran. UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said at a security forum in Bahrain on Sunday that there are no quick “off-ramps” through military solutions to the U.S. confrontation with Iran. Iranian negotiators are in Qatar discussing a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that no direct talks are happening with the U.S. Gargash acknowledged that the U.S. and Iran are far apart in their positions and warned of potential escalation if their differences aren't resolved.

articles.title: US Warns Iran Can't Hold Global Economy Hostage, Says 'Prepared To Go in Another Direction' if Hormuz Traffic Not Restored
articles.description: Addressing the Manama Dialogue security forum in Bahrain on Sunday, US Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs Donald Blome asserted that diplomatic pathways remain available, but cautioned that American tolerance is not limitless.
